title: Stress-slice convergence procedure for throughput benchmarking
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for a new throughput benchmarking harness mode we're calling 'stress-slice convergence'. The goal: get reproducible sustained throughput numbers while explicitly controlling for thermal drift, per-client pacing, and KV-cache state. It's built to catch run-to-run variance that standard steady-state runs sometimes hide.

Scope / when to use:
- Use when we need 95th-percentile confidence that observed throughput differences > X% are real (X configurable, default 5%).
- Use for multi-model fanout experiments, quantized vs fp16 path comparisons, and dedicated vs shared capacity claims.
- Not intended for short smoke tests — this is a controlled lab procedure for publishable claims.

High-level idea:
- Decompose a long run into repeated short "stress slices": each slice is a tightly-controlled burst + stabilization window.
- Between slices we run short cooldown/thermally-stabilize windows and optionally re-prime caches.
- Repeat across N independent seeds/anchor-client-shards and aggregate with robust statistics (median-of-means + variance decomposition).

Key telemetry to capture (recommend sampling 1s or finer):
- request rate / in-flight count / service RT metrics
- per-token cost counters and emitted token counts
- GPU telemetry: power (W), temperature (C), clock freq (core/mem), GPU util, memory used, ECC errors
- Host telemetry: CPU frequency, load, irq stats, net/rx/tx, NIC interrupts
- Runtime KPIs: kernel times, queue/batch sizes, KV-cache hit ratios, allocator stalls
- Process-level: GC/pool thrash, thread context switch rates

Loadgen config primitives (examples):
- client_shards: 8 (each shard pinned to a client host / process)
- slice_length_sec: 120  # raw measure window
- burst_profile: {"step_start_qps": 100, "step_incr_qps": 50, "steps": 6, "step_duration_sec": 10}  # implemented as synthetic ramp inside slice
- steady_slot_sec: 30  # last N seconds of slice used as stable sample
- cooldown_sec: 90  # quiet time after slice to let GPU T and clocks settle
- rng_mode: deterministic | stochastic  # deterministic uses fixed seeds for prompt selection
- kv_cache_mode: cold | warm | curated  # curated = prime with representative prefix set

Note: the harness accepts a YAML frontmatter with the above primitives; bench-runner converts the burst_profile to per-client pacing.

Repeatability hygiene:
- Clock sync: ntpd or chrony must be running and sync skew < 5ms across clients and servers. Add a pre-check step that fails the run if skew > 10ms.
- RNG: For deterministic runs set rng_mode=deterministic and store the RNG seed in run metadata. Also archive the exact prompt corpus used (hash + sample indices).
- Binaries: capture git SHA for runtime, compiler flags, cudnn/cuda/driver versions. Fail the run if driver version differs from baseline unless explicitly allowed.
- Thermal baseline: require at least one thermal-baseline slice after a cold boot to qualify the machine as "baseline ready". Record baseline idle GPU temp.

Thermal/clock handling recipe (why different from other warmup approaches):
- Measured problem: on some cards clocks scale up aggressively after sustained load which changes throughput profile mid-run. We therefore: 
  1) Start with an initial "heat-up" slice that ramps slower than production to let boost curves settle (example: step_incr_qps = 0.5x typical).
  2) After heat-up measure clock behavior for 60s; if clocks still trending, extend heat-up or trigger a cooldown cycle to re-align states.
  3) Use cooldown_sec windows to actively let temp drop ~5C (empirically reduces mid-run variance).
- Record whether we observed thermal hysteresis and tag run artifacts accordingly.

Statistical aggregation and checks:
- For each shard and each slice produce: median latency, 50/90/95/99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), batch_size distribution, and power mean/std.
- Use median-of-means across independent shards to get robust central estimate of throughput.
- Run a Levene test for equal variance across runs; if p < 0.05 flag non-homogenous variance and require more repeats or manual triage.
- For final claim, require at least 5 valid slices (post-triage) per configuration; prefer 9 for publication.

Automation-run checklist (pre-run):
1) Validate host/drivers/bench-runner SHA.
2) Validate SSH keys & client_shards connectivity.
3) Confirm chrony/ntp health and run clock sync check.
4) Ensure cooling room target is within +/- 2C of baseline.
5) Upload the prompt corpus snapshot and RNG seed to artifact store.
6) Start background telemetry exporters (node-exporter, nvml-exporter) and verify metrics ingestion.

Per-slice run order (explicit):
- slice_start: ramp according to burst_profile
- slice_measure: collect stable_slot_sec from the tail of the slice (discard earlier warm seconds)
- slice_end: stop clients, run quick health probe to check for OOMs or driver resets
- cooldown: idle period; optionally run small synthetic workload to maintain kernel residency but not raise temp
- archive: push artifacts (logs, perf counters, nvprof snapshots) to artifact store with slice metadata

Failure modes we look for (and triage notes):
- sudden throughput drop at a particular wall time across shards -> often network flakiness or firmware bug; check NIC error counters and dmesg.
- steadily increasing latency across the slice -> either thermal throttling or memory fragmentation; inspect GPU clocks and allocator metrics.
- wide shard-to-shard variance -> client pacing skew, clock skew, or nondeterministic prompt sampling; rerun with rng_mode=deterministic.

Examples / quick configs (copy-paste):
- short verification run (not for publish):
  client_shards: 4
  slice_length_sec: 60
  burst_profile: {step_start_qps: 200, step_incr_qps: 200, steps: 3, step_duration_sec: 6}
  steady_slot_sec: 12
  cooldown_sec: 30
  rng_mode: stochastic

- publishable config template:
  client_shards: 12
  slice_length_sec: 180
  burst_profile: {step_start_qps: 80, step_incr_qps: 40, steps: 8, step_duration_sec: 10}
  steady_slot_sec: 45
  cooldown_sec: 120
  rng_mode: deterministic
  kv_cache_mode: curated

Notes to self / open questions:
- How to codify "curated" KV prime corpora that are representative across model families? Need a small benchmark corpus curator service. (TODO: PROF-402)
- Investigate automated detection of "clock settle" events using the telemetry stream so we can auto-extend heat-up slices instead of failing runs.
- Consider integrating a quick P-state controller toggle to force clocks for controlled experiments (requires infra changes and safety checks).

Run artifacts and reproducibility pack (what to publish with a claim):
- bench-runner YAML, git SHAs, RNG seeds, prompt corpus hash, full slice telemetry (CSV), nvml logs, host dmesg, and a short human-readable summary with shaded regions called-out (thermal drift, net blips).

Quick triage flow when a run is flaky:
1) Re-run single shard with deterministic seed and watch telemetry live.
2) If clocks change mid-run, abort and mark as thermal issue; schedule longer cooldown and retest.
3) If only one host shows variance, repro on that host alone to isolate hardware/driver problems.

Appendix: quick commands (examples):
- ntp check: chronyc tracking && chronyc sources -v
- nvml stream dump (1s): python tools/nvml_stream.py --out run123_nvml.csv --interval 1
- artifact upload: tools/artifact_push --run run123 --files *.csv,*.log

If you use this procedure, please stash a copy of the run YAML in the "benchmark-claims" folder and ping #eng-benchmarks with the run id. I'm leaving a draft PR that wires the cooldown step into bench-runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner/pull/487 (WIP).

-- Asha
